title: What a weekly pool service visit actually covers
desc: What a Sunfish Pool Service tech does at a Sacramento pool every week, start to finish.
body: Here's what a Sunfish tech actually does at your pool every week.

You get a text when they're on the way. They test the water for chlorine, pH, alkalinity and calcium and balance it, then skim the surface, brush the walls and steps, empty the skimmer and pump baskets, and check the equipment while it's running.
When the work's done you get a photo of the pool and a water report sent to your phone. Same day every week, no contract.
That's the whole visit. Most of what makes it work isn't the checklist, it's doing it the same way every time so you stop thinking about the pool.
If you're in Sacramento, Carmichael, Citrus Heights, Antelope or Fair Oaks and want someone to take that over, we'll get you taken care of.

title: Fall leaf season in Sacramento and what it does to a pool
desc: Why October and November are the hardest months for a Sacramento pool, and what helps between visits.
body: Leaf season just started and it's the hardest stretch of the year for a Sacramento pool.

Leaves don't just float. They sink, they break down, and they pull chlorine out of the water while they do it. A pool that looked fine on Friday can be cloudy by Monday if the baskets fill up and the pump starves.
Here's what helps between visits. Empty the skimmer basket when you walk by, keep the pump running its full cycle, and don't shorten the run time to save power until the trees are bare.

We clear baskets and brush every visit, and in October and November we spend more time on it than any other month. The water report tells you when the chlorine is getting eaten, and that's your cue to call before it turns.
If your pool sits under trees, we'll get you taken care of.

title: Teaching techs so any one of them could run the company
desc: Why every Sunfish Pool Service tech learns the whole job, and what that means for customers.
body: Every tech at Sunfish gets taught the whole job, not just their piece of it.

That means the water chemistry, the equipment, how the route gets built, and how we talk to customers. It takes longer up front. A new tech rides along before he runs pools on his own, and that's a cost I pay on purpose.

Here's the reasoning. If any one of my techs could run the company for a week, nobody's pool gets skipped when somebody's out sick or on vacation. And when a tech knows what a pump should sound like, he catches the problem on a routine visit instead of the customer finding a flooded equipment pad.
The side benefit is I don't have to be on every call. The crew explains the problem in plain words, the customer gets a straight answer, and I get to work on the business instead of in it.
If you're in Sacramento, Carmichael, Citrus Heights, Antelope or Fair Oaks and want a crew that works that way, we'll get you taken care of.

title: Why we don't offer same-day or free anything
desc: The reasoning behind how Sunfish Pool Service runs its routes and prices its work.
body: We don't do same-day service and we don't do anything for free. Here's the reasoning.

A route works because every pool on it gets the same day, every week, and the tech knows what he's walking into. Same-day means pulling a tech off six customers who were promised today to get to one who wasn't. Somebody loses, and it's always the person who planned ahead.

Free is the same problem from the other side. A free first visit or a free estimate has to be paid for by someone, and that someone is the customer who stays. I'd rather tell you the number up front and let you decide.

It costs us some signups. People call wanting a pool fixed today, and I tell them we can get them on the route next week. Some hang up. The ones who don't tend to stay for years, because the same thing that kept me from dropping everything for them is what keeps me from dropping them for the next guy.
If you're in Sacramento, Carmichael, Citrus Heights, Antelope or Fair Oaks and want a company that runs that way, we'll get you taken care of.

title: Why we test the water every visit and what the numbers mean
desc: Chlorine, pH, alkalinity and calcium in plain words, and why Sunfish tests them at every visit.
body: We test the water at every pool, every visit. Here's why, and what the numbers actually mean.

Chlorine is what keeps the water safe and clear. Too low and algae gets a foothold, too high and it's harsh on skin and equipment. pH decides how well that chlorine works. When pH drifts high, the same amount of chlorine does a lot less.

Alkalinity is the buffer that keeps pH from swinging every time it rains or someone swims. Calcium protects the plaster and the heater. Too little and the water starts pulling it out of the surfaces, too much and it scales.
None of those numbers stay put. Sun burns off chlorine, leaves eat it, rain dilutes everything. Testing every visit means we catch the drift before it turns into a cloudy pool or a repair bill.
You get the numbers too. The water report lands on your phone after every visit, so you can see what we saw.
If you want someone keeping an eye on yours, we'll get you taken care of.

title: What communication means in practice: a text before, a note after
desc: What communication looks like on an actual service day at Sunfish Pool Service.
body: Communication is one of the three things Sunfish stands on, and I've learned that word means nothing unless you can point to what it looks like on a Tuesday.

For us it looks like this. You get a heads-up text when your technician is on the way, so a visit never surprises you. When the work is done you get a photo of your pool and a water report sent to your phone. Same day every week, so you know when we're coming.
That's it. No guessing whether we came by.

My crew does the hard part here, not me. A tech who takes the extra minute to write a clear note after a hot afternoon on route is the reason customers trust us. I just try to hire for that and get out of the way.
